## Proof

**Setup and notation.** Let

$$L_i \;=\; \log\frac{f(X_i;\theta_1)}{f(X_i;\theta_0)}, \qquad S_n \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^{n} L_i \;=\; \log\Lambda_n,$$

where $\Lambda_n = \prod_{i=1}^n f(X_i;\theta_1)/f(X_i;\theta_0)$ is the likelihood ratio. The Kullback–Leibler information is

$$I(\theta,\theta') \;=\; E_\theta\!\left[\log\frac{f(X;\theta)}{f(X;\theta')}\right].$$

Hence, defining $\mu_j = E_{\theta_j}[L]$ for $j=0,1$:

$$\mu_1 = I(\theta_1,\theta_0), \qquad \mu_0 = -I(\theta_0,\theta_1),$$

and by hypothesis $\operatorname{Var}_{\theta_j}(L) = \sigma_j^2 \in (0,\infty)$.

---

### 1. The MP test (Neyman–Pearson)

By the Neyman–Pearson lemma, the most powerful (MP) level-$\alpha$ test rejects $H_0:\theta=\theta_0$ in favor of $H_1:\theta=\theta_1$ when

$$S_n \;\geq\; c_n,$$

with the critical value $c_n$ chosen so that $P_{\theta_0}(S_n \geq c_n) = \alpha$.

---

### 2. CLT approximation under $H_0$ — determining $c_n$

Under $\theta_0$, the $L_i$ are i.i.d. with mean $\mu_0 = -I(\theta_0,\theta_1)$ and variance $\sigma_0^2$. By the CLT,

$$\frac{S_n - n\mu_0}{\sigma_0\sqrt{n}} \;\xrightarrow{d}\; N(0,1) \quad\text{under } \theta_0.$$

The size-$\alpha$ condition gives, for large $n$,

$$P_{\theta_0}\!\left(\frac{S_n - n\mu_0}{\sigma_0\sqrt{n}} \geq \frac{c_n - n\mu_0}{\sigma_0\sqrt{n}}\right) \;\approx\; \alpha.$$

Let $z_\alpha = \Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha)$ be the standard normal upper-$\alpha$ quantile. Then

$$\frac{c_n - n\mu_0}{\sigma_0\sqrt{n}} = z_\alpha \quad\Longrightarrow\quad c_n = n\mu_0 + z_\alpha\,\sigma_0\sqrt{n}.$$

**MP test (CLT approximation).** Reject $H_0$ when

$$\boxed{\;S_n \;\geq\; -\,n\,I(\theta_0,\theta_1) \;+\; z_\alpha\,\sigma_0\sqrt{n}\;}$$

or equivalently,

$$\frac{S_n + n\,I(\theta_0,\theta_1)}{\sigma_0\sqrt{n}} \;\geq\; z_\alpha.$$

---

### 3. CLT approximation of the power under $H_1$

The power is $\pi_n = P_{\theta_1}(S_n \geq c_n)$. Under $\theta_1$, the $L_i$ are i.i.d. with mean $\mu_1 = I(\theta_1,\theta_0)$ and variance $\sigma_1^2$. By the CLT,

$$\frac{S_n - n\mu_1}{\sigma_1\sqrt{n}} \;\xrightarrow{d}\; N(0,1) \quad\text{under } \theta_1.$$

Therefore, for large $n$,

$$\pi_n \;\approx\; P_{\theta_1}\!\left(\frac{S_n - n\mu_1}{\sigma_1\sqrt{n}} \;\geq\; \frac{c_n - n\mu_1}{\sigma_1\sqrt{n}}\right) \;=\; 1 - \Phi\!\left(\frac{c_n - n\mu_1}{\sigma_1\sqrt{n}}\right).$$

Substituting $c_n = n\mu_0 + z_\alpha\sigma_0\sqrt{n}$:

$$\frac{c_n - n\mu_1}{\sigma_1\sqrt{n}} \;=\; \frac{n(\mu_0 - \mu_1) + z_\alpha\sigma_0\sqrt{n}}{\sigma_1\sqrt{n}} \;=\; \frac{\sqrt{n}(\mu_0-\mu_1)}{\sigma_1} + \frac{z_\alpha\sigma_0}{\sigma_1}.$$

Since $\mu_0 - \mu_1 = -I(\theta_0,\theta_1) - I(\theta_1,\theta_0)$, we obtain

$$\frac{c_n - n\mu_1}{\sigma_1\sqrt{n}} \;=\; \frac{z_\alpha\,\sigma_0 \;-\; \sqrt{n}\bigl[I(\theta_0,\theta_1) + I(\theta_1,\theta_0)\bigr]}{\sigma_1}.$$

$$\boxed{\;\pi_n \;\approx\; \Phi\!\left(\frac{\sqrt{n}\bigl[I(\theta_0,\theta_1) + I(\theta_1,\theta_0)\bigr] \;-\; z_\alpha\,\sigma_0}{\sigma_1}\right)\;}$$

---

By the non-negativity of KL divergence and the identifiability condition $\theta_0 \neq \theta_1$ (in a regular family, distinct parameters give distinct distributions, so both KL informations are strictly positive),

$$I(\theta_0,\theta_1) + I(\theta_1,\theta_0) \;>\; 0.$$

$$\pi_n \;\to\; 1 \qquad (n\to\infty),$$

i.e., the MP test is **consistent**: its power approaches 1 for sufficiently large $n$.
